pages.name: Curate and Understanding split by job (proposal)
Cataloguing at scale: rules and arrivals

annotations.text:
Round: the side-by-side list answer, and the report record.

Read against origin/main 19f3733 — after #56, so the rail frame, the four states and the member-tree link are already built. This draws the half that is still open: the rail SENTENCE, and where a saved list lives.

#60 has since built the sentence — see REVIEW-RAIL-SENTENCE.md for the three copy defects.
The two numbers agree out loud: 32 in the rail, 32 in the pane, and "10 of 32 packed" says what the model actually saw. That clause is the provenance of the sentence beside it, not an apology.
One Record, two kinds. Curate's commit is the catalogue kind and already exists — append-only, server-stamped author, selection as a snapshot. A report is the same row with no steps.

The two calls handed back in FUNNEL-COST-IMPLEMENTED.md: where the wait/background choice goes on /next's one-click re-run, and §3 — keep-investigating offering the deeper surveys with the split price.

Read against main at 2d4357e.

Round one of the ports work. Read against origin/main 91d6d93.

Leads with a correction: the Curate column claims ports are derived from the accepted set. They are not — interfaces.propose() reads deployment artifacts at survey time and never consults a verdict.

And the scale finding: no human-accepted component is cohesive under any bar; curators accept named packages. So review happens at the branch.

The owner's round of 2026-09-14, points 1/2/3/6/7/9/10 — seven faces of one question.

Read against origin/main 0841c17.

The cause, from the code rather than the complaint: the Questions row renders the answer and cannot reach the members; Dashboard by-question renders the SAME sentence from the same envelope so it can host a detail disclosure whose payload opens in a 290px rail.

The owner's second round, 2026-09-15. Read against origin/main 93be502.

Point 3: the honesty rules made a surface scrupulous about what it cannot say and silent about what to do. The missing half is WHOSE absence it is.

Points 4/5/6 are one habit: a row composed from several analyses over several populations, written as though it came from one.

Item 1 of the work plan, ruled. Read against origin/main 05cb63c0 — after #104.

The question was unanswerable because three different things in this product are called "perspective": run_label (detect/coupling), Component.perspective (physical/deployment/logical/dev), and the twelve role chips in the chrome.

Ruling: a verdict is about the component — the thing at that path — not about the proposal that surfaced it. No schema change; four render changes and one sort change.

Item 2 of the work plan — the component branch tree, unblocked by the verdict ruling on page six.

The owner's point 4 is four questions in one: what this is, why we think so, how much of it you are seeing, and what you can do about it. The tree answers all four in the same rows.

Measured figures are from #85 on egeria-workspaces; the five branch rows are illustrative shapes, not spec. The artboard says which is which at the foot — a drawing should carry its own provenance.

Item 3 of the plan. Read against main at 7b7bc2b4.

Two halves. Selection is a control that already exists one level out — selectMode is resource-level in the sidebar; the tree has per-row accept and no way to act on several.

Blueprints are the live defect: the coverage sentence says '0 of 12 clusters in the logical reading reviewed' and blueprints have ZERO UI references in /next. A count that opens nothing.

And a blueprint verdict is reading-scoped (perspective::cluster_name) where a component's is path-scoped — one table, two identity regimes, and the screen has to say which.

Round 2 of the multi-resource brief, drawn against slices 6 and 7 as merged.

Every field name and all four state values are the shipped ones from database_column_profiles. stats_source and stats_computed_at are there because round 1 asked for them — the schema comment quotes the reasoning.

The third panel is not a design question: n_distinct is negative when it expresses a ratio, so the shipped REAL column will render "distinct: −0.8" unless the sign is branched on at the render site. Same shape as the counter-reset case.

Treemap deliberately not drawn — its inventory rows need checking the same way these fields were. The heatmap IS drawn, on page 10: slice 8 had landed in #193, which I only found on looking.

Round 2, second drawing. Read against main at 9d531b3b — slice 8 (postgres_operations, #193) had already landed, so the role side exists and this was drawable after all.

Drawing it found three separate paths by which the grid can say "no access" about a role that has access:

1. Cells are inherited from TABLE grants. role_table_grants is table-level and database_grants has no column_name, so a column-only grant (GRANT SELECT (email)) is invisible. Ask: read information_schema.column_privileges — a strict superset — and add column_name. A migration, which is why it belongs in round 2.

2. PUBLIC is a pseudo-role, so it cannot be one column among five. It is a band above the grid.

3. Role membership is read nowhere — no pg_auth_members, no pg_has_role. Granting through a group role is normal Postgres administration. has_column_privilege() answers all three at once.

The rule the page turns on: for an exposure view the two failure directions are not symmetric. An empty cell must mean "no path found", never "no path".

Round 3. Read against main at 9bc1c153 — slices 9, 10 and 12 merged.

Both round-2 items were fixed, and the n_distinct fix went three corrections deep, catching the reltuples provenance and the PG13 sentinel ambiguity I had not seen.

Two findings:

1. The DRAFT badge is correct in classic, including the part nobody asked for — an empty contentStatus draws no badge because 'not stated' is not 'confirmed'. /next has no Egeria annotation surface at all, so the divergence is permitted today and becomes a silent omission the day that pane is built. And amber cannot port: /next has three audited state roles and no room for a fourth. DRAFT is not a state — it says who has agreed so far, orthogonal to ok/warn/gap — so it is an ink chip, not a colour.

2. The n_distinct fix correctly refuses to guess, returning None — for four different reasons, on a row still labelled state = measured. A wrong number became a blank that cannot say why. The live case: pg_stat_reset() clears last_analyze while pg_stats survives, so after a reset every near-unique column loses its distinct count on a healthy database. stats_reset is already in scope at database_surveyor.py:379 and is not consulted.

Heatmap: wait. The next drawing depends on which of the two grant fixes is taken. But the shipping rule is settleable now — it must not ship caveated, because a caveated exposure grid is still read as a grid.

Designer round 2 on the database screens. Read against main at 019c2796 (#318) and the owner's screenshots of 2026-09-27.

Three things in the screenshots are already fixed in code: tree order, kind words, the filter's expanded-empty table.

The finding under all three items: there are already three glyph tables (GLYPH, factGlyph, CELL) that disagree, and the brief would add a fourth. One table, one module; the glyph names a family, the word names the state.

A prerequisite for the tree overview: 'empty' folds four conditions, including never-measured, stored as row_total 0. A row-count bar built on it draws 'not measured' as 'counted, zero'.

The per-schema overview goes into the tree's rows rather than a second chart, with rows AND columns: column counts come from the catalog, so a structure-only credential still gets a real bar.

Header: each line leads with its state; only the remedy is in the accent colour. Neither remedy exists in /next today.

Drawn from the 91 real AdventureWorks edges, fetched 2026-09-28 from the running /next through the owner's session. Laid out with Graphviz dot; nothing illustrative.

Three zoom levels: the schema map (always legible), the whole database (reads at 68 tables thanks to clusters, hub weight and darker cross-schema keys; falls back to map + hubs above ~100), and one schema opened with its outgoing keys drawn.

Finding: the analysis's by_schema result calls sales.salestaxrate and sales.shoppingcartitem isolated and sales '3 components'. Both have keys that leave the schema; only production.transactionhistoryarchive is isolated in the database. A per-schema sentence must say 'no keys inside sales', never 'isolated'.

In /next: emit Graphviz rather than Mermaid (Kroki renders both; Mermaid has no cluster layout comparable to dot).

Reply to ASK-DESIGNER-ENRICHMENT-STAGE-IA, read against main at 3d078072 and PR #348.

Enrichment opens on a new Context tab: everything a person supplied, signed and dated, each row saying what it feeds. No separate 'What it changed' tab — cause and effect on one line.

No analysis in the catalog has intent: enrichment, so Survey & analyses is empty by construction; it stays, and becomes the map of which analyses elsewhere read what is supplied here.

A survey may propose only an observation, and only when it measured the same fact the field asks for. Licence yes; last backup no (archiving isn't a tested restore). Judgements are never proposed.

The lens belongs to the investigation, not the resource.

Prerequisite: answers to the human questions carry no author and are entered via window.prompt().

Reply to ASK-DESIGNER-WORK-LISTS-VS-INVESTIGATIONS (#354), read against main at 8c6f1845.

Not one mechanism: an investigation's scope is a Folio (working_sets); a work list is a separate table (work_lists), one resource type, published as a WorkingSet.

'Work list' names four things: the bench, its shortlists, a one-resource list minted by 'add to work list' on reports and member lists (the owner's trigger), and the suggested-to-* inboxes.

Ruling: investigation = why; scope = which (any type; 'Members' becomes 'Scope'); work list = the bench only. 'Working set' never on screen.

Two actions on the list: add to <investigation>, start an investigation from this list. The list stays, linked, and says '7 of 9 in scope' live.

The investigation page carries the grid, one per resource type; a scope narrows by verdict, a list by shortlist.

Questions 5-8 (addendum, against fffcc3a0), lower artboard:
5. A stage click: run stages keep the list and re-scope its questions; Investigation, Understanding and Automate close it into 'back to'; Investigation with a linked list opens that investigation.
6. The data lens sits between purposes and scope; rows signed, literal-or-reference in words; undeclared dimensions on one line.
7. Fit row = one equal-width cell per declared dimension. Fits ✓, doesn't fit ∅ (not ✕), couldn't check ?, no reader yet ◌. Headline counts sum to the declared number. Verdicts are the existing dispositions; 'archive' is a finding, not a verdict.
8. Pair questions in their own 'Between resources' section, one row per pair, both names bracketed; parity per question.

Replies to ASK-DESIGNER-CURATE-AND-UNDERSTANDING-ALL-KINDS and ASK-DESIGNER-DISCOVERY-SOURCES-ALL-KINDS, against main at 524f1c7f.

Curate, every kind: Findable (group, tags) → the kind's own work → what people say (ratings as counts, never an average; the signed journal as notes, Classic's unsigned curator notes read-only beneath). Tags, feedback and notes record no author today: add one.

Understanding, database: Now (schemas, largest tables by rows, column types) and Over time (since last run as a sentence, structure over runs, activity per table). The chart routes read the old blob and turn unestablished row counts into 0: rebuild on database_tables.

Chart kinds per kind; per-chart Save image with provenance in the image.

Find: three surfaces and a CSV contract already exist (Admin sources, Find repos, Find databases, batch_io). One Find dialog per kind: Saved sources, one-off search/discover, From a file; one confirm that can add to an investigation. Non-connectable databases listed, not filtered. CSV rows name a server, never a credential.

Reply to ASK-DESIGNER-RESOURCE-CONTROLS-PLACEMENT, against main at cf52f4a9.

The top bar's resource name is drawn like a control (accent border) and isn't one: make it the resource's menu (hide, remove). Remove is last, after a rule, in ink; its confirmation opens under the bar and the commit button names the resource.

The header keeps the disposition pill; hide and remove leave it.

Select: a labeled control, shift/⌘-click entry, 'select these N' on a filtered list. The bar is grouped by weight: scope, judgement and lists, view, then remove after a rule.

One word: 'Remove from Resource Explorer'; 'delete' retired. Find gets a word: '＋ Find databases'.

Reply to ASK-DESIGNER-CURATE-CATALOGUE-SCOPE-DATABASES (and the coco_pharma addendum), against main at 45f4671b.

The scope is a declared, signed, dated choice stored in RE; the commit compiles it into the cataloguer target's include/exclude lists every time, so a reset and re-commit restores it.

Band 2 order: what gets catalogued, then glossary terms, then schema match. Depth before the tree; the column-depth offer after commit, once.

Proposals only when the decision follows from a measurement alone: 0 tables, no writes since, a lens match. PII is a mark; a staging-like name is a note. Four observation states fit. Undecided keeps what's in Egeria; only an explicit leave-out removes.

Per-node state from proof: catalogued (read back), attached · waiting, queued, failed, left out. Name-filter conflicts block the commit before the press. The manifest names RE's publish, the cataloguer, and the native survey (which measures what you left out too).

Round 2 (lower artboard, against e1770aec): facts only from stored rows, each sourced and dated; activity is active / dormant / can't tell from the cumulative counters since stats_reset, with the window printed, and can't-tell proposes nothing. A filter offers a bulk choice now or a rule that keeps deciding; precedence hand > rule > schema > undecided, each row says which. Return visits open on what changed since the last commit. No survey records 'worth cataloguing'; the Schema Inventory tab on any stage writes the same scope events. Lens terms in names become a suggested rule, not a proposal.

Replies to ASK-DESIGNER-STATE-AS-VISUAL-CUE and ASK-DESIGNER-VERBS-UNMAPPED-CONTROLS Q7, against main at f1f679eb.

The cue sits where the decision was made; the sentence is one gesture away; a pressed control looks pending and ignores a second press; a control that changes nothing visible is not a control.

Two lanes: your choice (fill = chosen value in ink, lowered row = not included, tag = source, edge rule = needs you) and in Egeria (glyph + word). Strike-through means superseded text only.

Scope row choice is a selector, Include | Leave out, under 'Include in catalog?'; Catalog appears only on the commit button. Steps become a numbered stepper with 'step n of 9 · running · failed'. The manifest becomes a table per mechanism with the Catalog button on top and blockers under it.

Reply to ASK-DESIGNER-CURATE-SPLIT-BY-JOB (a proposal), against main at 62bcd4ad.

Three jobs as Curate's stage-specific leading tabs on the existing sub-tab rail (the Context precedent), not a third level of tabs: Describe and publish · Contents · Structure. 'What it is' moves to Structure. No mode; a saved landing tab; counts on tab names.

A running commit shows as one line on every tab, the stepper only where pressed. Tab 1 is the non-expert seed; Forget links, project bind and copy GUID move to Contents. A database has one press (Catalog) on Contents; tab 1 shows its state.

Understanding: same positions (whole / parts / detail), names At a glance · Contents · Over time; both stages say 'Contents' at position 2.

Reply to ASK-DESIGNER-CATALOGUING-AT-SCALE, against main at 08390160.

Egeria catalogs whole schemas today (one schema-kind target per schema, no lists: S1, S11), so a schema rule acts and a table or column rule is kept for when Egeria can (owner, 2026-10-15).

Rules are signed events in the scope record, listed in a strip with their match counts; the filter bar is the editor; a hand choice overrides one row and says it differs from the rule.

Arrivals: a new schema waits for Publish; a new table in a published schema is added by Egeria's cataloguer on its own refresh, said in Egeria's name; a gone table stays, lowered, until read back.

Reply to ASK-DESIGNER-RUNS-REGISTRATION, against main at df5dbc91.

One survey definition, one card: its runs (whoever coordinated them) move onto the definition card; RE definitions leave "Egeria's own surveys". One verb, Run, with the coordinator named: "Re-run…" and "Re-run · coordinated by Egeria →". A definition Egeria cannot start shows the control off, with the step named.

A refusal the person can fix says how on the run line; ○ not run replaces ⊘ refused. Registration states come from what Egeria answered: will change, couldn't connect (naming the address), no longer in Egeria (one press to register again). The signed-in user is never truncated.

Replies to ASK-DESIGNER-TABLE-PREVIEW and ASK-DESIGNER-GROUP-SCHEDULING-AND-FIRST-INDEX (2026-10-19), against main at 55c5c6ea.

A preview is an act, not a view: nothing runs until the press; the header says whose credential, how many rows, not a sample. Masking reasons sit on the column header (PII match, confidential, not profiled); reveal is one column, one confirm, one audit row.

Scheduling: the form is always visible with a For picker (resource, selection, Group). A selection is a bulk choice; a Group schedule is a rule that follows membership. Own schedule beats Group. First index asked first, with measured and estimated figures each sourced, one confirm per batch.

Plan for bordered cards and big-number tiles (PLAN-CARDS-AND-TILES), after the owner's users voted for the Dark look, 2026-10-20.

A card is one thing to read or act on: header with actions top right, body, provenance footer. One level only; a list is one card. The left edge means needs-you and nothing else.

A tile is one count that is the answer: it opens what it counted, reads the same field at the same precision as the place it opens, and shows absence as a state (? not read, ○ not measured, ◐ partial), never 0. Slices C1 to C4, starting with At a glance and Survey & analyses.
